capabilities.need: a. Full-screen insert shots that leave the chat UI for 1-4 beats on a keyword hit and come back
capabilities.exists: Two routes work today. (1) Insert as its own shot: src/scenes/shot.js sequence() (l.20-64) has no minimum length; the film already runs 1-beat shots (count-1..6, 0.462 s) and 1.5-beat ones (c2-complete, err-breath, exec-12, 0.692 s). The engine keeps two content layers (engine.js l.54-55, A outgoing / B incoming) plus one overlay layer. Nothing is stored between frames, so 'returning to the same UI state' just means a second shot def that calls the same draw closure with the same camera function. (2) Insert inside one shot: draw a full-frame plate after ctx.camera() and bring it in through a moving clip. 11_count.js does exactly this (masked l.154, wedges l.156, blinds l.160, interleave l.164, shutter l.196-203, counter roll l.212-218, punch-in with ghosts l.245-247), each finished in 0.10-0.12 s. A shot's palette may be a function (t,f,u), so the state palette can switch for the insert frames.
capabilities.gap: No helper splits a UI shot around inserts. Constraints for route 1: cuts must sit within 2 ms of a half-beat (tools/storyboard.mjs l.63), so the shortest grid-legal insert shot is half a beat (0.2308 s, 13-14 frames); every def needs its own `moment` (l.64) and its lines covered. Overlaps are clamped to the room between cuts (shot.js l.30-39, console.warn when shortened), so for an insert of length D, in-transition dur + out-transition dur must be <= D. A lead-in (align 'end') renders the returning shot at t < at. Anything keyed on u.at / u.since / u.k, or on enter() tied to the new def's cut, restarts on return: UI code must key on absolute times (T(i), Bt(n)). KIT section 1 requires every lyric line readable for its whole sung duration, so a plate that hides the thread must carry the line or keyword itself. No reusable textured dark ground exists outside room(): dots() (11_execution.js l.96) and hatch() (12_outro.js l.54) are section-local, and grain exists only in post (uniform).
capabilities.suggested_approach: Add two small pure helpers to src/scenes/kit.js. (1) withInserts(uiDef, inserts): returns [ui part, insert, ui part, ...]; each ui part reuses uiDef.render / camera / palette but passes the ORIGINAL u (recomputed from the original at/until), ids suffixed -a/-b, lines split. Use it for departures of 1 beat or more that want shader transitions and their own palette. (2) plate(ctx, t, { at, dur, in, out }, draw): in-shot full-frame plate with canvas wipes lifted from 11_count.js (iris via arc clip, wedges, blinds, interleave, shutter, punch-in). Use it for flashes under 1 beat or off the half-beat grid. Add a ground(ctx, opts) in a new src/components/plate.js: panel fill + ctx.radial light pool + dot grid or hatch + huge faint spark + a seeded noise tile built once at load (prng.rand into an offscreen canvas at device resolution, used via createPattern) + registration marks. An overlay-scene route (an extra { overlay: true } scene in index.js) is possible but worse: fx.hud scales it, the storyboard does not list it, and the bloom background stays that of the shot underneath.

capabilities.need: b. Flat three-ink silhouette art: load, split into ink plates, recolour, offset, reveal separately, mask, clean fringe, scale crisply above native
capabilities.exists: art.js loads only the six names in ART_NAMES (l.19) from config paths.art; _prepare (l.42-73) builds gray / inv / sil (alpha matte) / blur canvases and a 160x240 luminance map. art.silhouette (l.120-127) gives one flat colour from the alpha matte. art.duotone (l.130-142) maps luminance continuously to two roles: orange ink (luminance about 0.5) becomes a muddy half-mix, so it is not ink separation. exec-07 (11_execution.js l.305-317) already fakes misregistration with offset art.silhouette copies. Measured on the 13 supplied PNGs (4 female, 3 boy, 3 adult, and 圖片/Claude猫耳娘/猫耳娘1-3.png, which already exists): 1086x1448 (female no.1 is 1254x1254); three clean inks, black about (36,26,21), orange about (217,112,62), cream about (242,224,198), per-channel sd 3-20; 1.4-4.5 % of visible pixels are anti-alias mixes; alpha ramp about 1.3-1.9 px.
capabilities.gap: No loader for the new files, no colour classification, no per-plate drawing, no fringe cleaning, no crisp upscale. The fringe is real: per image, 14-23 k dust pixels at alpha <= 0.02, 50-270 pure-red and up to about 290 white stray pixels at low alpha, and 1-5 islands of 1-2 px. art.silhouette magnifies the native matte with smoothing, so edges go soft; art._check warns above 1.75x at 4K, i.e. a whole image wider than about 950 virtual px. A bust 1080 virtual px tall at 4K is already 1.49x native. LUM map and regions.json assume the old 2:3 art; the new files have no regions. Black ink is almost the page colour (on.bg #262624), so black faces and clothes merge into the ground unless there is a plate, light pool or keyline behind. File names contain CJK and spaces.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Copy the files used into assets/silhouette/ with ASCII names and list them in config.json. Extend Art in src/engine/art.js rather than adding a new env key: tools/storyboard.mjs l.18 stubs only `art`, so a new key would silently send sections to the fallback in the storyboard run. One-off in _prepare: getImageData at load (never per frame); membership = alpha > 0.5; label each pixel by nearest ink centroid in RGB (seed with the three measured colours, refine per image); drop components under about 30 px. That removes all dust and stray hues. Build plates cumulatively in print order so no seams show and misregistration reveals the ink below: cream = whole silhouette, orange = orange + black, black = key plate. Crisp upscale: draw each mask at U x (U = 2 or 3 from a per-image maxScale in config) with smoothing, then re-threshold alpha with a steep ramp around 0.5 and store the plate canvas. Memory is 25 MB per plate at 2x (75 MB per image), so prepare only the images used; skip gray / inv for flat art. If close-ups above 2x are wanted, trace the label map to Path2D per ink (marching squares on the soft membership, light simplification, even-odd): crisp at any scale, clip-able, stroke-able, negligible memory. API: art.inks(ctx, name, dst, { roles: { cream: 'text', orange: 'me', black: 'panel' }, offset: { orange: [dx, dy] }, reveal: { cream: k, ... }, alpha, crop }) and art.inkMask(ctx, name, ink, dst, fn) to clip fn to one plate. Tint in a tmp canvas at destination device size (source-in), as silhouette() does. Keep a 1/3-resolution label map (Uint8Array) per image for glyph and dot sampling. Roles follow the palette, so `off` greys the figure for free.

capabilities.exists: art.ascii (art.js l.179-200): one glyph per cell from the 160x240 luminance map, default size 16 (cell 9.6x16), ramp ' .:-=+*#%@', three colour tiers at k 0.33 / 0.66, clipped to the dst rectangle only. Its only use in v3 is exec-04 (11_execution.js l.218, size 12, cell 7.2x12, over a dim duotone print). shapes.asciiFill (shapes.js l.113-148): fills a 180-point outline on a grid anchored at (cx,cy), default size 20 (cell 12x20), ramp ' .:o0#', a shade(nx,ny,col,row) callback for procedural brightness, top-down reveal, and it IS clipped to the outline with the even-odd rule. SHAPE.eggplant / tomato / cat (l.55-57) are the simple v2 spline blobs. ascii.js has asciiSphere (lit globe with noise continents, graticule, reveal, dissolve) and asciiBursts. asciiFill, asciiSphere and asciiBursts are unused in v3.
capabilities.gap: Confirmed on a rendered frame (151.3 s): art.ascii reads as coarse blocks with horizontal banding, because the nearest-neighbour luminance map is coarser than the glyph grid; there is no edge awareness, no dithering, no outline clip. asciiFill at size 20 gives only about 55x33 cells for a 300 px shape and no internal structure unless shade() invents it, hence 'blobby'. No image or shape can be sampled to edge-aware characters today. Both helpers call g.fillText directly, skipping ctx.text's glyph check, so a ramp with block or box characters would silently fall back to a system font. asciiSphere / asciiBursts default to legacy roles dim / mid / fg, which alias to grey and cream, not orange.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Add glyphPlate() to src/engine/ascii.js, driven by the label map and plates from (b) or by a procedural field. Glyph size 9-11 (full frame at size 10 = 320x108 cells; still row-batched: one fillText per row per tier or weight). Supersample each cell 2x3 for coverage and shape. Interior cells: density ramp per ink, with separate ramp and colour per plate (black = sparse dots in meDim, orange = code glyphs in me, cream = dense glyphs in text), so colour separation carries the picture. Boundary cells: pick / \ | - _ ( ) < > ' , from the local edge direction (Sobel on the label map). Use mono weights 300 / 400 / 700 / 800 as extra brightness tiers. Draw dense regions from a real token stream (the lyric's own code words) instead of a random ramp. Clip the grid to the plate silhouette (inkMask or Path2D) for a crisp contour, add a 1-2 px keyline, and keep a dim flat print underneath as exec-04 does. Animate with a row-print reveal or per-cell decode keyed rand(key, i, j, floor(t*12)), held 5 frames or more, never reshuffled per frame. For eggplant / tomato, replace the blob outlines with multi-part implicit shapes (body, calyx, stem, highlight as separate inks) shaded per cell with rim light. Stay inside the bundled glyph set and lower fx.glow (x0.4-0.5) over large glyph fields.

capabilities.need: d. Pure code / terminal look without the chat chrome

Post scanlines: config post.scanlines 0.03 x fx.scan, 360 lines. Section-local precedents: boot log() (01_boot.js l.24), requestBlock (10_error.js l.99), the mono code block in v1-points.

capabilities.suggested_approach: New src/components/code.js, all pure functions of t. codeBlock(ctx, rect, lines, { size, numbers, hl: lineIndexAt(t), tokens }) with roles: keyword = me, string = text, comment = mute, rest = sub. terminal(ctx, rect, entries[{ at, text, tone }], t, { rows, size }) where scroll = max(0, shown(t) - rows) * lineHeight, eased per line, inside ctx.clip. counter(ctx, x, y, n(t)) with a digit roll as in 09_alone.js count() (l.50-58). stack(ctx, rect, depth(t)) pushing frames until it overflows the rect. For the EXECUTION loop: the highlighted line bounces inside a short while-loop, one console line and one counter tick per shout, stack depth growing; ground = room({ motif }) or the plate ground from (a), fx.scan raised to about 3-5. The number cards after it can reuse the same mono / terminal styling so the two parts match.

capabilities.need: e. Strong light: bloom, glow, flash, rays, streaks, exposure
capabilities.exists: post.js: 5-level bloom pyramid (LEVELS l.139; half resolution per level, 9-tap separable blur). The first downsample gates by saturation (config glow.satKnee [0.28, 0.62], FS_DOWN l.48-51) and subtracts the palette background (l.53). Composite adds bloom * palette bloom tint * 0.42 * uGlow, with uGlow = (fx.glow + flash * 0.8) * palette.glow (l.311). fx.glow defaults to 0.55 + 0.2 * lowEnv; scenes only lower it (0.12-0.75); there is no upper clamp. Palette glow: off 0.45, on 1.0, warm 1.25, error 1.1, errRed 0.35, errCream 0.2, ash 0.6, dead 0.3. ctx.flash(v, role) / enter.flash: capped at safety.maxFlash 0.7, times post.flashStrength 0.5, slightly centre-weighted (FS_COMP l.134). fx.bright = whole-frame exposure multiplier (l.133, not capped). ctx.glow(color, radius, fn) = canvas shadowBlur halo, the only glow for cream / grey. ctx.radial, ctx.gradRect. Section-local rays() (08_chorus2.js l.125) and motif.burst() are drawn lines.
capabilities.gap: No light rays, no anamorphic streak, no lens flare, no standalone radial / zoom blur; the only radial blur is inside the `zoom` transition (transitions.js l.118-134, 8 taps, only during a shot overlap). No exposure bloom on cream: cream saturation is about 0.02, well under the knee, and the knee is a global config constant, not a per-frame fx. Raising fx.glow above about 1.2 clips large orange areas towards the peach bloom tint, not white.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Add to defaultFx() (engine.js l.74-89; numeric fields are blended automatically by blendFx) and FS_COMP: (1) fx.bloomAll 0..1 + fx.bloomThreshold: in FS_DOWN mix the saturation gate towards 1 and apply a luminance threshold of about 0.25-0.35, giving cream and white bloom for the climax only (2 uniforms). (2) fx.streak 0..1: sum 8-12 horizontally offset taps of bloom levels uB2 / uB3, tinted: anamorphic streak from textures that are already small. (3) fx.rays 0..1 + fx.raysAt [x, y]: 12-16 taps of uB1 / uB2 marched towards the centre with decaying weight: light rays from whatever blooms, cheap at 4K because the sources are 1/2-1/4 resolution. (4) fx.zoomBlur 0..1 + centre: 8-12 taps of uBase along the radial direction: speed blur for the time-travel shot and for impacts. (5) optional flare ghosts: 3-4 taps of bloom at mirrored, scaled uv. All stateless. In canvas, additive light cones and ray fans can be drawn with ctx.g.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter' / 'screen'.

capabilities.need: f. Glitch toolkit: what each does, ranges, local use, stutter
capabilities.exists: ctx.fx, all whole-frame, in FS_COMP order: glitch 0..1 (l.89-94): 28 bands, about 28 % slide sideways up to +-6 % of width (+-115 px at 1.0), pattern held 6 frames; scenes use up to 0.54, pulsed on bar downbeats (10_error.js tear() l.357-361). mosaic = cell size in virtual px, with optional fx.mosaicRect [x, y, w, h] (l.97-99). mosh 0..1 (l.102-113, 122-126): 80 px blocks smear one displaced column, quantise to 4 levels, 14 % swap channels (c.gbr), 26 % fill with palette err colour; reshuffles every 16 frames; about 25-30 % of blocks at 0.5, about 80 % at 1.0. rgbSplit in px horizontal (scenes 0.4-3). aberration, radial (default 0.0005, under 1 px). desat 0..1, invert 0..1, shake [x, y] px (scenes 5-7), rot, zoom. Transitions `glitch` and `slices`. In canvas: type.js sliced(), art.slices(), the exec-11 band shuffle (11_execution.js l.446-452), 04_pre1.js mosaic(ctx, cell) (l.80-91: pixelates what is drawn so far, later drawing stays sharp), ctx.trail ghosts, thinking({ stuck }).
capabilities.gap: Only mosaic can be limited to a rectangle. Nothing can be limited to one layer: the post pass runs after A + B + overlay are merged, so the overlay glitches too. mosh, mosaic, invert, desat are never used in v3, so they are untested there. mosh's channel swap turns orange into blue / violet, breaking the colour rule. There is no feedback buffer by design, so no accumulating datamosh or video echo. No engine-level frame repeat.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Stutter, repeat and time-slice are all possible deterministically because every draw is a pure function of t. Hold: tq = floor(t * n) / n. Stuck loop (for the broken LOVE syllables): tl = t0 + ((t - t0) mod len). Add timeWarp(def, map) to kit.js: wraps render, camera and palette with tm = map(t) and features f.src.sample(tm) (sample() returns src). Slit-scan: draw the scene function N times, each clipped to a strip, at t - i * dt (N x canvas cost). Local glitch: add glitchRect(ctx, rect, t, { bands, amount, split, hold }) to type.js or a new src/engine/fxcanvas.js: self-copy of the layer region through a scratch canvas (the 04_pre1.js mosaic pattern), band offsets from rand(key, band, floor(t * 60 / hold)) with hold of 6 frames or more. Cheap shader additions: fx.glitchRect uniform (same test as uMosaicRect), block-quantised displacement, vertical roll, a `moshKeep` switch that drops the gbr swap.

capabilities.need: g. Time effects for the A.D-to-B.C image
capabilities.exists: The current pre1-date shot (04_pre1.js l.401-420, band() l.251-288; 52.04-55.73 s): a timeline band across the frame, the two era tokens in 204 px serif either side of a line, a mono year readout rolling from A.D. to 3000 B.C. via readout(u) (l.57-58), tick ruler, the spark as the dragged knob with ctx.trail(6, 0.014) ghosts and ctx.glow, a burst on the crossing. Reusable: ctx.trail (draw.js l.348-356), numeral echoes (11_count.js drawNumeral l.50-58), count() digit roll (09_alone.js l.50-58), type.onPath (text on a circle or spiral), scramble for digits, shapes morph / trace, geom.js wireframes (MESH, rot, project, drawSegs), asciiSphere with rotY (shared.js worldRotY), fx.rot / fx.zoom / fx.aberration / fx.rgbSplit.

capabilities.suggested_approach: Keep the band and add depth behind it inside the same shot (or as a 2-beat insert): a tunnel of receding frames or rings with z = (i + speed * (t - t0)) mod N, speed following the drag, seen through fx.zoomBlur from (e); an odometer with per-digit columns rolled by ctx.trail; arcs via ctx.circle(a0, a1) whose length follows speed; fx.aberration ramped to about 0.004-0.008 and a few degrees of fx.rot during the pull; asciiSphere spinning backwards. Era markers as flat three-ink cut-paper polygons in the style of the new art (geometric subjects only: skyline, columns, pyramid), passing in parallax and misregistered while moving. A sun to moon morph with shapes.morph also serves the a.m / p.m line later.

capabilities.need: h. Transitions: which exist, and which can run inside one shot
capabilities.exists: 15 shader types in transitions.js (list in transitions_available), chosen by the incoming shot's enter: { type, dur, align 'end' | 'start' | 'center', x, y, color, flash, flashColor, flashDecay }. v3 uses only cut (64 shots), fade (6), push (5), zoom (3), scan (2), glitch (2), slices (1). In canvas, inside one shot: the 11_count.js set (shutter, counter roll, 12-wedge sunburst, 16-column blinds, 9-band interleave, punch-in with ghosts), the 04_pre1.js mosaic, the exec-11 band shuffle, type.sliced, and any ctx.clip / ctx.clipPath mask (SHAPE outlines or motif.sparkOutline as an iris).
capabilities.gap: No shader transition can run inside one shot: each needs two layers, i.e. two shots. No enforced minimum duration, but there is a practical one per type. circle, diag, grid, shatter, dissolve, winclose, winpop, flashcut have never been used in v3. The engine `push` eases in, so it cannot leave exactly on an off-beat (the reason count-2 draws its own). flashcut and every edge highlight default to cream (pal.accent, transitions.js l.62) unless color: 'me' is given.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Promote the 11_count.js helpers (masked, wedges, blinds, interleave) plus an arc iris and a shape iris into kit.js as part of plate() from (a). Use shader transitions only for departures of 1 beat or more: winpop, zoom, circle and slices suit 'into a graphic and back'. For the lead-in from the trance line into the next section, a 1-2 beat `zoom` or `dissolve` with align 'end' fits the existing overlap rules.

capabilities.need: i. Photosensitivity limits for a brighter, glitchier climax
capabilities.exists: tools/check_flash.py measures an exported 60 fps mp4 (details in flash_safety). Engine guards: safety.maxFlash 0.7 on ctx.flash; glitch pattern held 6 frames, mosh 16 frames, transition glitch 8 frames; each glitch / dissolve block switches once; the warning toast shows for the first 6.5 s (overlay.js).
capabilities.gap: No current measurement of v3 exists: the README status section is an empty placeholder and the only mp4 (out/preview_1080p60.mp4, 19:44) is older than every v3 scene file (21:08-22:23). fx.bright, fx.invert, flashcut, light plates, bloom and any new light fx are outside the maxFlash cap. The README names 2:28-2:57 as the flashing range; a stronger second chorus (163-193 s) widens it.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Budget the climax as at most 6 large-area luminance swings per rolling second, cuts included: one light hit per beat at most, sustained brightness instead of pulsing, glitch holds of 6 frames or more, inserts of 3 frames or more. After building, export 1080p60 and run npm run check; update the README range and status numbers.

capabilities.exists: Three Latin roles and four CJK roles, loaded before the first frame (engine.js loadFonts l.19-45); ctx.text reports any glyph outside the bundled set (draw.js l.194-206). Details in font_and_glyph_limits.
capabilities.gap: No arrows except up / down, no heart, tick, infinity, pi, no box-drawing or block characters, no mono or sans italic, CJK limited to six strings.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Draw symbols as shapes (SHAPE.heart, polyline tick, iconButton). For ASCII ramps stay within ASCII + Latin-1. If Greek letters are wanted, load the -greek- files in loadFonts and extend the LATIN set in draw.js. The S / M letter design needs nothing new: all Latin, with ctx.at scale / rot and per-letter drawing as slam() does.

capabilities.need: k. Performance and determinism at 4K60 with heavier effects
capabilities.exists: Every frame is renderFrame(t) only. 2D layers are bit-identical for a given t; the GPU passes may differ by 1/255 on up to about 0.02 % of bytes (post.js l.219-223). README: full 1080p60 export takes about 13 minutes on this machine (about 16 fps). Glyph grids and layouts are in virtual 1920x1080 units, so loop counts do not grow at 4K; raster, upload (3 canvases per frame), readPixels and the frame pipe do.
capabilities.gap: 4K export time is not measured; my estimate from the 1080p figure is 30-55 minutes (4x pixels through raster, 3 texture uploads, readback and a 33 MB frame over the socket). Costly patterns: per-glyph fillText (asciiSphere dissolve style) at tens of thousands of glyphs; ctx.trail(n) and slit-scan re-render the scene n+1 times; both shots render during every overlap; the shatter transition takes 50 samples per pixel; large ctx.glow radii.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Do all pixel classification and plate building once at load; never call getImageData on a layer per frame (it forces GPU readback and can switch the canvas to CPU raster mid-export, changing anti-aliasing). Avoid per-frame g.filter; if used, multiply radii by ctx.scale, as for shadowBlur (filter and shadow units ignore the transform). Build noise tiles at device resolution. Keep ASCII row-batched. Key every hold on floor(t * 60 / n) or on beat time, never on call order. Memoise only pure results keyed by all inputs (as `measured` in draw.js does). Keep new shader loops to 16 taps or fewer and sample bloom levels instead of the full-resolution base where possible.

capabilities.need: l. Timing of keyword hits for graphics that flash in on the beat
capabilities.exists: cues(): T(i) line start, H(i) snapped to a half-beat, B(n), Bt(b) with fractions, P = 0.4615 s. 49 ALL-CAPS lines are flagged emphasis and snapped to the beat within 0.06 s (lyrics.js l.13). features.onsetsIn(t0, t1, minStrength) gives detected onsets with strength (1060 in the file); f.beatPulse, f.barPulse, f.onsetPulse.
capabilities.gap: data/lyrics.json has line times only (129 lines, no word timestamps). Concrete nouns inside a normal line (eggplant, tomato, tabby cat, the era tokens, a.m / p.m and so on) have no time of their own.
capabilities.suggested_approach: Place each noun hit on the grid by ear with Bt(...) and check with contact sheets; or pick the strongest onset inside the line's window with features.onsetsIn(T(i), lyrics.end(i), 0.35) and snap it with features.snapHalf. Keep every hit on a beat or half-beat so in-shot plates and insert shots agree.

transitions_available: cut (type 0): instant. Optional flash / flashColor / flashDecay (default 8, visible about 0.3 s) on any type. 64 of 83 shots use it.
fade (1): plain dissolve, eased. Any duration; the film uses 0.5-2 beats.

glitch (2): 12x7 blocks and 22 rows switch A to B once each; torn rows shift up to +-15 % of width, re-rolled every 8 frames; +-23 px colour split peaking mid-way. Used at 0.5 beat, align start. Practical minimum about 0.15-0.25 s.
scan (3): scanline wipe, dir 0 down / 1 up / 2 right / 3 left, hot edge line plus striped trailing band, eased. Used at 1 beat. Minimum about 0.2 s.
circle (4): iris from x,y (inverse: true closes) with a thin bright ring, eased. Minimum about 0.15-0.2 s. Unused in v3.
diag (5): 16-slat diagonal wipe with edge glow, eased. Minimum about 0.2 s. Unused in v3.
grid (6): 16x9 cells open in a diagonal cascade, linear. Minimum about 0.25 s. Unused in v3.

zoom (7): fly-through: outgoing picture scales to 10x with an 8-tap radial blur and fades while the incoming grows from 12 % size at x,y (out: true reverses). Used at 1-2 beats. Minimum about 0.3 s. The incoming picture reads as a growing rectangle.
shatter (8): outgoing picture breaks into 90 falling triangular shards that brighten as they go. Minimum about 0.4 s. Heaviest shader (50 samples per pixel). Unused in v3.
dissolve (9): random pixel blocks flip once, size parameter, edge tint on fresh blocks. Minimum about 0.15 s. Unused in v3.
winclose (10): outgoing picture collapses to a line, then to a point at x,y (CRT off); incoming fades up behind. Minimum about 0.25 s. Unused in v3.
winpop (11): incoming picture pops up from x,y with overshoot and a thin border; outgoing dims to 40 %. Minimum about 0.12-0.2 s. Unused in v3.
push (12): both pictures slide, dir 0 left / 1 right / 2 up / 3 down, eased (so it cannot leave exactly on an off-beat). Used at 0.5 beat.
slices (13): `bands` (default 10) horizontal slices of the outgoing picture slide off alternately left and right with staggered starts. Used at 0.5 beat, align start. Minimum about 0.2 s.
flashcut (14): hard switch at mid-point under a full-frame colour bloom (strength 0.85). Default colour is cream and it is NOT capped by safety.maxFlash; it counts as a flash. Unused in v3.

In canvas, inside one shot (11_count.js): dark shutter split (l.196-203), counter roll (l.212-218), 12-wedge sunburst wipe (wedges l.156), 16-column blinds (blinds l.160), 9-band interleave (interleave l.164), numeral punch-in from 220 % with ghost frames (l.245-247); each finishes in 0.10-0.12 s.

In canvas, other: 04_pre1.js mosaic(ctx, cell) (l.80-91); the exec-11 band shuffle (11_execution.js l.446-452); type.js sliced(); art.slices(); any ctx.clip / ctx.clipPath mask, including SHAPE outlines and motif.sparkOutline as an iris; shape-to-shape match cuts with shapes.morph across a hard cut.
post_fx_available: fx.flash via ctx.flash(v, role) or enter.flash: additive colour, capped at safety.maxFlash 0.7, times post.flashStrength 0.5 (at most about +0.34 at centre, +0.24 in the corners); also lifts bloom by flash * 0.8.

fx.glow: bloom strength, default 0.55 + 0.2 * lowEnv, multiplied by palette.glow (0.2-1.25); scenes use 0.12-0.75; no upper clamp. Only saturated colour blooms (config glow.satKnee [0.28, 0.62], global, not per frame).
fx.bright: whole-frame exposure multiplier, default 1; not capped by the flash guard.
fx.zoom, fx.rot (radians), fx.shake [x, y] in virtual px: whole-frame camera; outside the picture is black.
fx.rgbSplit: horizontal red / blue separation in px (scenes 0.4-3). fx.aberration: radial separation, default 0.0005 (under 1 px at the edge).
fx.glitch 0..1: 28 bands, about 28 % of them slide sideways up to +-6 % of width; pattern held 6 frames (0.1 s). Scenes use up to 0.54, pulsed on bar downbeats.
fx.mosaic (cell size in virtual px) with optional fx.mosaicRect [x, y, w, h]: the only effect that can be limited to a rectangle. Unused in v3.

fx.mosh 0..1: 80 px blocks smear a displaced column, drop to 4 colour levels, 14 % swap channels (orange turns blue / violet), 26 % fill with the palette's err colour; reshuffles every 16 frames. Unused in v3.
fx.desat 0..1 (to luminance grey) and fx.invert 0..1: whole frame. Unused in v3; the cold grey look at 113 s is the palette blend warm > off, not desat.
fx.scan and fx.vignette: multipliers on scanlines (0.03, 360 lines) and vignette (0.34). Film grain 0.028 is always on.
fx.hud: opacity of the overlay layer (warning toast, credits).

Not available in post: light rays, anamorphic streak, lens flare, standalone radial / zoom blur, luminance (cream) bloom, feedback / echo, per-layer or per-rect effects other than mosaic. Every post effect also hits the overlay layer.

Canvas-side light and glitch: ctx.glow(color, radius, fn) local halo (the only glow for cream and grey), ctx.radial, ctx.gradRect, ctx.trail(n, dt, fn, strength) ghost samples, type.sliced, art.slices, art.halftone / duotone / ascii / silhouette, 04_pre1.js mosaic, raw globalCompositeOperation 'lighter' / 'screen' on ctx.g.
flash_safety:
WHAT THE CHECKER MEASURES. tools/check_flash.py reads an exported mp4 (use 60 fps; npm run check points at out/preview_1080p60.mp4), scales it to 64x36 by area averaging, and works per pixel.

- General flash (l.72, transitions() l.29-47): relative luminance from linearised sRGB. A pixel marks a transition each time it has moved 0.10 or more of full scale away from its last extreme, in the opposite direction to its previous move, and only when the darker of the two states is below 0.80. Two transitions make one flash.
- Area and rate (flashes_per_second l.50-57): in every 60-frame window it takes the transition count reached by the busiest 25 % of pixels (75th percentile) and halves it. FAIL above 3 flashes, i.e. 7 or more transitions in any second for a quarter of the frame. The quarter need not be the same pixels at the same instants.
- Red flash (l.76-78): only pixels with R / (R+G+B) >= 0.8 count, with value (R-G-B) * 320/255 and a transition threshold of 20/255; same area and rate rule.
- Informational: count of hard frame changes (mean abs diff > 0.12) and the busiest second; single-frame pops (a frame differing by > 0.05 from both neighbours while the neighbours are alike).
- It is an approximation of WCAG 2.3.1, not a certified PSE test.

WHAT TRIPS IT.
- Cuts count: a cut between a dark shot and a light field (errCream, a cream plate) is one transition for every pixel that changes; cutting back is the second.
- A full-strength capped flash is about +0.34 sRGB at centre and +0.24 in the corners. On the empty dark UI that sits right at the 0.10 threshold (cream flash 0.7 counts almost everywhere; the peach default only in the centre; flashes of 0.45 or less do not count). Over lighter content the same flash clearly counts.
- None of the palette reds is 'saturated red' by this measure (err is 0.56, errRed background 0.68). What produces it is channel separation: a large fx.rgbSplit (beyond about 8-10 px) on big bright type, or mosh channel swaps.
- PLAN section 9 lists what failed in practice: large saturated red type or bars that move fast, glitch patterns reshuffled every frame, amounts that pulse with the beat.
- Outside the 0.7 cap: fx.bright, fx.invert, the flashcut transition (cream at 85 % by default), light plates, bloom, and any new rays / streak fx.

WHAT A BRIGHTER, GLITCHIER CLIMAX MUST RESPECT.
- Budget: at most 6 large-area luminance swings per rolling second, cuts and flashes together. At 130 BPM one hit per beat is 4.3 transitions per second (pass). A rise-and-fall pulse on every half-beat is 8.7 (fail). Dark / light alternation on half-beats is 4.3 (pass, little room left). Anything on quarter-beats fails.
- Steady brightness is not a flash. The section can sit much brighter (higher fx.glow, sustained fx.bright, luminance bloom) if it gets there in one move and stays; each change of direction is what costs.
- Do not hold fx.glitch high over large bright content (its pattern changes at 10 Hz) and do not combine continuous mosh (3.75 Hz) with per-beat flashes over the same area.
- Keep glitch and stutter holds at 6 frames or more; no insert or flash shorter than 3 frames (the pop detector); no invert toggling; no strobing of anything over a quarter of the frame.
- Keep rgbSplit small on large type, or apply it to thin elements only.
- No valid measurement of v3 exists yet: the only mp4 predates the v3 scenes and the README status block is empty. Export 1080p60 and run the check after the climax is rebuilt, then update the README warning range (currently 2:28-2:57) to include the second chorus.
font_and_glyph_limits:
FAMILIES AND WEIGHTS LOADED (config.json fonts, engine.js loadFonts l.19-45; latin subset files only).
- mono = JetBrains Mono 300 / 400 / 700 / 800, no italic. Advance is 0.6 em (ctx.cw).
- serif = Source Serif 4 400 / 600 / 700 / 900, italic 400 / 600.
- sans = Inter 400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800, no italic.
- Any other weight falls to the nearest loaded one; italic on mono or sans is a synthesised slant. More weights and italics are in node_modules/@fontsource (JetBrains Mono 100-800, Source Serif 4 200-900, Inter 100-900) and need only a config entry.
- Roles are fixed: serif = the AI speaks, sans = interface and user, mono = system and code.

GLYPHS THAT CAN BE DRAWN (draw.js LATIN l.35-36): ASCII; Latin-1 from U+00A0 to U+00FF except the soft hyphen (includes ¦ § © « ¬ ° ± ² ³ µ ¶ · » ¼ ½ ¾ ¿ × ÷); ı Œ œ; a few modifier marks and combining accents; – — ‘ ’ ‚ “ ” „ • … ′ ″ ‹ › ⁄ € ™ ↑ ↓ −.

GLYPHS THAT CANNOT: → ← and every other arrow, ♥, ✓, ∞, π and all Greek, ≠ ≤ ≥, box-drawing and block elements (─ │ █ ▓ ▒ ░), braille, emoji, any dash or space from general punctuation not listed above. None of the fontsource subsets of JetBrains Mono contains box or block characters, so an ASCII ramp must be built from ASCII and Latin-1. Greek exists as a separate subset that is not loaded.

HOW MISSES ARE HANDLED. ctx.text reports a console error once per string and the glyph falls back to a system font. art.ascii, shapes.asciiFill and ascii.js call g.fillText directly and skip that check: a bad ramp character would fall back silently and break the 0.6 em grid.

CJK. Noto Serif / Sans KR and TC are linked through their package CSS and only the configured strings are preloaded: 넷, 한국어, 六, 中文 (roles krSerif, krSans, tcSerif, tcSans; one weight each, 700 serif / 500 sans). ctx.text on a CJK role reports any other character. More CJK text means extending fonts.cjk[].text in config.json; Japanese has no package installed.

Fringe on the supplied PNGs is visible on a dark ground if drawn untreated: 14-23 k near-transparent dust pixels and a few hundred stray red / white low-alpha pixels per image. Classification at load removes them; plain art.draw would not.

Memory: Art._prepare makes three full-size derived canvases per image. Loading all 13 new files that way is about 330 MB on top of about 150 MB for the old six; 2x re-thresholded plates add 75 MB per image. Load only the images used and drop gray / inv for flat art.
File names of the supplied art contain CJK characters and spaces; copy to ASCII names under assets/ rather than pointing config at 圖片/.

4K60 export time is unmeasured (my estimate 30-55 minutes from the 1080p figure). ctx.trail, slit-scan and overlaps multiply canvas cost; per-frame getImageData or canvas filters on a layer would be slow and can change rasterisation mid-export.

The GPU passes are not bit-exact between two renders of the same frame (1/255 on up to about 0.02 % of bytes, post.js l.219-223). Glitch and grain patterns key on round(t * 60) mod 4096, so they wrap every 68.3 s; harmless, but do not rely on frame-exact pattern identity across exports.
